value.body: A two-year master's in psychology, usually with a specialisation such as clinical, counselling, organisational (industrial) or social psychology. A general MA or M.Sc does not by itself make you a licensed clinical psychologist; that needs a professional programme recognised by the Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI).

items.label: Course length
items.note: Often includes a dissertation and fieldwork

items.label: PG enrolment in psychology
items.note: All PG years, as reported to AISHE
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, PG enrolment by subject, based on actual responses (Ministry of Education)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A BA or B.Sc, usually with psychology (some universities accept other graduates). Admission is through CUET-PG at central and many state universities, or a university or institute entrance test. To register with the RCI as a clinical psychologist, you need an RCI-recognised professional course with its own entrance.

value.title: At a glance
items: Working as a clinical psychologist in hospitals requires RCI registration; many counselling, HR and research roles do not.
Supervised practice hours and further training shape counselling and clinical careers.
Teaching and research posts usually need UGC-NET and a Ph.D.

value.title: Postgraduate students in Psychology
value.note: All postgraduate psychology enrolment, not only clinical or RCI-recognised programmes; forensic psychology is counted separately. AISHE counts only responding institutions, and coverage varies by year.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, Table 13 (PG enrolment by discipline, 'Psychology' row), actual responses (Ministry of Education)
